definition: Intractable means so stubborn that attempts to manage, control, or solve it keep failing.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word intractable. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know intractable should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The young colt proved so intractable that he bucked off every saddle and ignored every command the ranch hands tried.
A stubborn problem resists a first attempt or two; an intractable one defies every method anyone throws at it.
Ungovernable is stronger than intractable, describing something so far beyond control that no authority can restrain it at all.

Unmanageable means impossible to handle or control; the word announces that management has failed. It is the plainest twin of intractable and often interchangeable with it. Intractable adds a sense of active, continuing stubbornness: every new method gets tried, and every method gets defeated.

Unruly means hard to control and disorderly, and it describes behavior: an unruly crowd, an unruly mane of hair. Unruly things can usually be settled by a firmer hand. An intractable problem or person defies every method of control anyone applies, firm or gentle.

Obstinate describes a person digging in, stubbornly refusing to change course or cooperate on some particular point; it is willful by definition. Intractable reaches wider, covering problems, conflicts, and pain as well as people, and it points at the failure of every attempt to manage them.

The community garden's bamboo patch proved intractable: volunteers cut it, dug out the roots, and smothered the bed with tarps, yet new shoots kept spreading into the neighboring plots.
The bamboo resists every method the volunteers use to control it and keeps spreading anyway.
Something that stubbornly defies all attempts to manage or contain it is exactly what intractable describes.
Intractable commonly pairs with problem, conflict, and pain, and it can also describe a person or animal that refuses to be guided.

Keep it distinct from insoluble, which applies only to a problem or dispute that has no solution at all: an intractable situation resists every attempt to manage or control it, even if a solution might exist in theory.

Ravenna's downtown traffic has humbled four mayors in a row.
The first widened the avenues; gridlock returned within a year.
The second synchronized every signal; the jams simply moved two blocks north.
Free shuttle buses, congestion fees, one-way conversions -- each fix arrived with fanfare and failed within eighteen months.
Planners now describe the congestion as intractable, a problem that has absorbed every method the city can devise and given nothing back.
A visiting engineer put it more gently: some problems are not puzzles waiting for the right key, she said, but conditions a city must learn to live with.
